subject: Biology
title: Mitochondria: The Powerhouse
description: A fast breakdown of Mitochondria: The Powerhouse for builders.

hook.text: Mitochondria burn glucose with oxygen and produce ATP, the energy currency of life.

buildup.text: Each human cell holds hundreds to thousands of mitochondria, based on energy demand.

discovery.text: Mitochondria have their own DNA—a circular genome inherited only from your mother.

twist.text: Billions of years ago, a larger cell swallowed a bacterium. They partnered instead of fighting.

climax.text: That ancient partnership still runs. Every breath you take fuels your mitochondria.

punchline.text: A swallowed bacterium still powers your body.

quiz.question: Where does mitochondrial DNA come from?

details.summary: Mitochondria are double-membrane organelles that generate most of a cell's ATP through cellular respiration. They have their own DNA and reproduce independently within cells, remnants of ancient bacteria that were engulfed by an ancestral cell in an endosymbiotic event.
details.whyItMatters: Mitochondria produce roughly 90 percent of cellular energy. Mitochondrial dysfunction is linked to aging, neurodegenerative diseases, and metabolic disorders, making them central to both health and disease.
takeaways: Mitochondria generate over 90 percent of cellular ATP energy
They carry their own circular DNA inherited exclusively from the mother
The endosymbiotic theory explains their origin as engulfed bacteria

faq.question: Why do mitochondria have their own DNA?
faq.answer: Mitochondria evolved from free-living bacteria that were engulfed by an ancestral cell about 2 billion years ago. They retained their own circular DNA genome, similar to bacterial DNA, as evidence of this ancient endosymbiotic partnership.

faq.question: Why is mitochondrial DNA only inherited from the mother?
faq.answer: Sperm contribute almost no cytoplasm and few if any mitochondria during fertilization. The egg provides virtually all mitochondria to the embryo. This maternal inheritance makes mitochondrial DNA useful for tracing maternal lineage in genetics research.
